full_judgment: 8. Plaintiffs now claim that by way of settlement and successive transfers from the Azmot Ali Kha taluk they have acquired title in the suit lands. On the other hand, they claimed that the then Government handed over some lands in favour of Golam Gafur Sawdagor. If the suit lands were settled to Golam Gafur and Asgor Ali by registered deed, how the Government gave possession of some lands out of the said lands to Golam Gofur again is not clear to us? It is also not clear to us how the Government has taken over possession of the remaining lands and handed over possession of additional lands to Zila Parishad? The plea of taking over lands as excess is an absurd story in that, before the promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SA & T Act) there was no law authorising the Government to take over possession of lands from any individual as excess lands other than by way of acquisition. All rent receiving interests of persons who have been described as rent receivers in clause (23) of section 3 of SA & Act, i.e., rent receiving interests of (i) proprietors (ii) tenure holders (iii) raiyats, (iv) under-raiyats (v) non-agricultural tenants in some cases, (vi) landlords in respect of service tenures (vii) lands in khas possession of rent receivers (viii) hat or bazar, (ix) fishery and (x) forest, etc. have been acquired on and from the date of publication of Gazette Notification dated 14th April, 1956. Admittedly, the suit lands had been recorded in the RS Khatian No. 981 in the name of the Zila Parishad and thus the lands vested in the defendant prior to 1950. Plaintiffs claim that the defendant petitioner has settled 0.58 acres of land out of 8.28 acres of land to Noor Hossain and, on the other hand, they have claimed proprietary right in the said lands, which claims are self contradictory. This inconsistency has cropped up after introducing the story of settlement by Exhibit 1 in order to avoid the plea of res judicata.
